headline: Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it interferes with Iran deal
summary: US President Donald Trump warned Oman that it would be bombed if it 'gets in the way' of a deal regarding the Strait of Hormuz.
details: US President Donald Trump has threatened to bomb Oman if the country 'gets in the way' of a deal with Iran concerning the control of the Strait of Hormuz.
In an interview with Fox News journalist Trey Yingst, Trump stated, 'If Oman gets in the way, we’ll bomb the s*** out of them,' referring to ongoing talks between Oman and Iran.
The US President also called for Iran to 'put up the white flag of surrender' and reiterated on Truth Social that Iran must not be allowed to possess a nuclear weapon.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei accused the US of violating the Islamabad MoU, stating that a 60-day period linked to a June memorandum between Tehran and Washington is no longer relevant.
In other regional developments, the Yemeni army reported the launch of two hypersonic ballistic missiles by the Houthi group toward the Red Sea and Mocha city.
Additionally, two drones targeted the office of the Kurdistan Regional Government’s prime minister in northern Iraq, though no casualties were reported.
Trump also instructed the Pentagon to substantially reduce joint military exercises with South Korea, citing high costs and Seoul's refusal to take action against Iran.
caption:
“If Oman gets in the way, we’ll bomb the s*** out of them.”

US President Donald Trump has threatened to bomb Oman if the country 'gets in the way' of a deal with Iran concerning the control of the Strait of Hormuz.

In an interview with Fox News journalist Trey Yingst, Trump stated, 'If Oman gets in the way, we’ll bomb the s*** out of them,' referring to ongoing talks between Oman and Iran.

The US President also called for Iran to 'put up the white flag of surrender' and reiterated on Truth Social that Iran must not be allowed to possess a nuclear weapon.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei accused the US of violating the Islamabad MoU, stating that a 60-day period linked to a June memorandum between Tehran and Washington is no longer relevant.

In other regional developments, the Yemeni army reported the launch of two hypersonic ballistic missiles by the Houthi group toward the Red Sea and Mocha city.

Additionally, two drones targeted the office of the Kurdistan Regional Government’s prime minister in northern Iraq, though no casualties were reported.

Trump also instructed the Pentagon to substantially reduce joint military exercises with South Korea, citing high costs and Seoul's refusal to take action against Iran.

headline_marked: Justice AKM Asaduzzaman [[appointed as ACC chairman]]
headline: Justice AKM Asaduzzaman appointed as ACC chairman
summary: The retired Appellate Division judge leads the reconstituted anti-graft body, joined by two new commissioners.
details: Justice AKM Asaduzzaman, who retired from the Appellate Division in February, has been appointed as the chairman of the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC).
Along with the chairman, former secretary Jahangir Alam Khan and former National Board of Revenue tax commissioner Md Sazzad Hossain Bhuiyan have been appointed as ACC commissioners.
The appointments were made under the ACC Act 2004, as detailed in a notification signed by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani.
Under the Act, the ACC chairman receives salary and benefits equivalent to a Supreme Court Appellate Division judge, while commissioners receive benefits equivalent to a High Court Division judge.

The anti-graft watchdog had been without commissioners since March 3, following the departure of former chairman Mohammad Abdul Momen and commissioners Mia Muhammad Ali Akbar Azizi and Brig Gen (retd) Hafiz Ahsan Farid.
caption:

The appointments were made under the ACC Act 2004, as detailed in a notification signed by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani.

Under the Act, the ACC chairman receives salary and benefits equivalent to a Supreme Court Appellate Division judge, while commissioners receive benefits equivalent to a High Court Division judge.
